analysis: All three changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/inference.md, model-autopilot.md, telemetry.md), so no executable behavior or security control changed in this PR. In inference.md the only head-side change is the date bump and one Failure-modes row (line 2316) saying an unexpired Autopilot placement hold can refuse a cold load with a 503 or insufficient-memory error. The rest of the supplied inference.md text is unchanged context and I did not treat it as new. model-autopilot.md (head lines 22-24, 32-121, 129-130) documents adoption and hold placements and the busy-reason and transition-watchdog behavior. It states several security-relevant properties: adoption grants serving only, with no prefetch, publication or revision changes; placements end on consent revocation, deselection, residency loss, failed self-test or unverifiable weight hash; placements are in memory only; the watchdog cancels only a stalled operation and releases no native memory fence; and a coordinator uses these features only for providers reporting matching `capabilities`. These claims fit the TB-011 / A-016 serving-authorization model, since leased control is still required for operations and ordinary load safeguards remain in place. Documented residual risks are availability only: a held slot can block cold loads (T-029-style monopolization), but it is bounded by `hold_seconds` expiry and the holds are coordinator-driven under a lease. telemetry.md adds typed heartbeat fields (`busy_reason`, `busy_reasons`, `busy_since_ms`, `transition_stalls`) and says no prompt or completion content is added; this is consistent with the A-001 and T-058 identity-leak concerns. The Autopilot source files (ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift, TransitionWatchdog.swift, etc.) and the protocol reference were not supplied, so the doc claims are unverified. No concrete regression is identified. The next pass should confirm the code matches the stated invariants, in particular that adoption does not bypass `autopilotAllowsModel` or weight-hash verification.
